question: Name the organization that made the Golden Quadrilateral Project connecting major cities of India feasible?
solution:
The correct answer is __**National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Golden Quadrilateral project was spearheaded by the **National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)**, an autonomous agency under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
 
• It is a highway network that connects four major metropolitan cities of India—**Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata**.
 
• This ambitious project was initiated under **Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee's administration** as part of the National Highways Development Project (NHDP).
 
• The Golden Quadrilateral spans approximately **5,846 kilometers** and is one of the largest highway projects in the world.
 
• The NHAI was responsible for planning, construction, and maintenance of this network, ensuring improved connectivity and faster transportation across India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)**

 
 
• Established in **1988** under the National Highways Authority of India Act, 1988.
 
• It is responsible for the development, maintenance, and management of national highways in India.
 
• NHAI operates under the **Ministry of Road Transport and Highways**.
 
• The agency ensures seamless connectivity and oversees mega infrastructure projects like NHDP, Bharatmala Pariyojana, and other national highways.
 
 
 
• **Golden Quadrilateral Project**
 
 
• The project was implemented to enhance **economic growth and reduce travel time** between major cities.
 
• It is part of the **Phase I of the National Highways Development Project (NHDP)**.
 
• The road network connects cities in a quadrilateral shape, ensuring efficient transportation and trade.
 
• Key benefits include reduced fuel consumption, improved logistics, and enhanced industrial growth.
 
 
 
• **National Highways Development Project (NHDP)**
 
 
• Launched in **1998**, it aimed at upgrading and expanding India's national highway network.
 
• NHDP includes multiple phases such as the Golden Quadrilateral, North-South and East-West Corridors, and other projects.
 
• It is managed by the **NHAI** and funded through government allocations, loans, and toll revenues.
 
• The project has significantly improved India's transportation infrastructure and connectivity.
 
 
 
• **Bharatmala Pariyojana**
 
 
• A more recent initiative aimed at **developing highways for seamless connectivity across India**.
 
• It focuses on corridor-based approaches, rural road connectivity, and border area infrastructure.
 
• Managed by NHAI, Bharatmala Pariyojana is a step forward from NHDP to address emerging infrastructure needs.
 
• The project envisions improving logistics efficiency and reducing transportation costs across the country.
